Plugin Reference > node — Node.js Compatibility Facade

node — Node.js Compatibility Facade

Zig 0.17This plugin is built with Zig 0.17: the 0.17 branch builds successfully with Zig 0.17 and passes the Zig unit tests; the old 0.14.1 branch is left untouched.

sa_plugin_node rewrites common Node.js modules as a native SA C-ABI surface: in the words of its API_COVERAGE.md, it is "a native SA compatibility layer for common Node.js APIs. It does not execute JavaScript and does not depend on Node, V8, or VM APIs" — it does not execute JavaScript, does not embed V8/VM, and does not invoke the node executable. This page explains where its scale comes from, how to choose between its two return-type conventions, what each module surface offers, how far its protocol support goes, and what is explicitly out of scope.

NoteThis directory has no README. The authoritative sources, in order, are sap.json (capability sections and permissions), node.sai/node_extra.sai (ABI contracts), api.md (target module list + protocol matrix), API_COVERAGE.md (implemented surfaces and exclusions), and progress.md (module progress ledger). All figures on this page are labeled with their source and date basis.

1. Positioning and Scale: Where the 1,160 Externs Come From

api.md itself is not a symbol catalog; it consists of two parts: the first half is a list of target surfaces organized by the chapters of the official Node.js documentation (Asynchronous context tracking, Buffer, Child processes, Crypto, DNS, File system, HTTP, Net, OS, Path, Process, TLS/SSL, URL, Utilities, Zlib, etc., 63 lines), and the second half is a network protocol capability matrix (a static verification of the four plugins' source on 2026-07-03; see Section 5 below). Three chains actually land that list onto symbols:

  1. Module roster: progress.md tracks by the caliber of “public top-level facade modules that are not VM/V8”, self-rating 43 / 43 modules complete (100%). Its caliber note states: the denominator excludes internal path variants such as path/posix, dns/promises, and fs/promises.
  2. Contract generation: node.sai (287 lines, 235 @extern) + node_extra.sai (926 lines, 925 @extern), totaling 1,160 externs (measured for this page with grep -c '@extern'; the evaluation document “Four-Plugin Evaluation”, 2026-06-15, records the same figure).
  3. A four-piece set per module: most top-level modules carry a set of self-describing helper exports, <module>_status_json / _exports_json / _config_json / _feature_support_json, used to report at runtime what that module “has implemented and has not implemented”. This is one of the main reasons the extern total swells into the thousands.

2. The Six Skills and the Host Permission Boundary

sap.json declares six capability sections: node.os, node.process, node.crypto, node.net, node.dns, and node.http. The manifest gives no mapping table of “which skill corresponds to which symbols”; docs/dependency_refactor_plan_cn.md only mentions that node.http/node.https/node.net are application-layer semantics, with the lower layer going through http-client / http-server. Use sa skills --json to confirm whether these sections are loaded.

The permission ledger (the permissions field of sap.json, enforced by the host) determines what each module can actually touch:

DimensionDeclared contentImpact on each module surface
fsFive operations each on $PROJECT/** and /tmp/**: read / write / create / delete / metadataReal reads and writes by fs.* and vfs are limited to these two roots; the paths in tests are indeed temporary files such as /tmp/sa_node_fs3.txt
netOnly http://127.0.0.1:18395 and http://localhost:18395 Outbound connections by net/dgram/tls/http are constrained by this; the purpose of port 18395 is not explained in any document (the evaluation document notes that it is hardcoded and that multiple instances will collide on the port)
envHOME, TMPDIR, TMP, TEMP, SA_* process.env.get/set/delete and environment_variables can only reach allowlisted variables
process"spawn": true, with an exec allowlist of only /bin/echo and /usr/bin/echo (arguments unrestricted) Real child processes from child_process/cluster can only run echo; the evaluation document takes this as evidence that child_process is not yet truly usable

On dependencies, sap.json declares dependencies on http-client and http-server (both ABI 1). build.zig compiles those two plugins' http_saasm_api.zig directly into libnode.so, consistent with API_COVERAGE.md: "HTTP/1 client … by compiling the official http-client and http-server plugin implementations into libnode.so".

3. The u32 / u64 Dual Convention and the Selection Rule

The two contract files have different return-type conventions; this is the most important rule for using this plugin:

  • node.sai — the main module surface, returning a u32 status code. For example (verbatim): @extern sa_node_plugin_fs_read_file(path_ptr: ptr, path_len: u64, &out_ptr: ptr, &out_len: ptr) -> u32
  • node_extra.sai — the extended module surface (fd-level fs, promises, tls, sqlite, vfs, ffi, web_*, http/2/quic/dtls, worker_threads, child_process, cluster, etc.), returning u64. For example (verbatim): @extern sa_node_plugin_tls_connect(host_ptr: ptr, host_len: u64, port: u64, servername_ptr: ptr, servername_len: u64, reject_unauthorized: u64, &out_socket: ptr) -> u64

Selection rule: importing the single file node.sal is enough. Its header is @import "node.sai" + @import "node_extra.sai", and it contains all 929 extension macros in full (same-named macro bodies are verbatim identical to node_extra.sal; this page compared NODE_CRYPTO_CREATE_HASH). node_extra.sal is only a standalone copy of those 929 extension macros; do not import it together with node.sal, or macro names will be defined twice.

The two macro classes have different parameter styles, which must be distinguished when writing calls:

  • Main macros use a named “outputs first, inputs after” style. NODE_FS_READ_FILE expands to %out_ptr, %out_len, %out_status, %path, %path_len, internally using stack_alloc for output slots, then call, then load back.
  • Extension macros use a mechanically generated positional style, with parameters simply %p_0, %p_1, …, in an order strictly equal to the .sai signature order. NODE_CRYPTO_CREATE_HASH %p_0, %p_1, %p_2, %p_3 corresponds to a sa_deno…-style signature (algo_ptr, algo_len, &out_state_ptr) -> u64: p_0/p_1 are the algorithm string pointer and length, p_2 receives the state handle pointer, and p_3 receives the u64 status code. Before using an extension macro, always check the signature in node_extra.sai to confirm the argument order.

5. Protocol Matrix Boundaries: What Is Truly Supported and What Is Only a Shell

Each row below is taken verbatim from the "Network Protocol Capability Matrix" in api.md (labeled "verified 2026-07-03, code-static", a static verification conclusion over the sci + four plugins' source; “truly supported” = runnable end-to-end, “shell” = ABI + capability gate only):

Protocol layerCompletenessEvidence path (verbatim from api.md)
TCP socket / UDP socket / IPv4-v6 addresses✅ Truly complete (provided by sci net.sa) sci/sa_std/net.sa; sci/src/runtime/sa_pthread_host.c
DNS✅ ABI (basic resolution)node_extra.sai 127-175
HTTP/1.0, HTTP/1.1 client + HTTPS (TLS 1.2/1.3 client)✅ Truly supported sa_plugin_http_client/src/http_saasm_api.zig; node_saasm_api_ext.zig:529 std.crypto.tls.Client.init
WebSocket (RFC6455)✅ Truly supported (frames self-implemented at both ends) http_saasm_api.zig WebSocketHandle/maskInPlace
HTTP/2 (h2c client subset + server handshake)✅ Truly supported; complete server response ❌; over-TLS (ALPN) ⚠️ half-connected, requires manual assembly node_saasm_extra.zig:5563; Nghttp2Api; no nghttp2_session_server_new/submit_response
HTTP/3❌ ABI shell only (send/recv is raw UDP, not H3/QPACK frames) node_saasm_extra.zig:6286 http3_session_send_datagram == dgram_send_connected
QUIC❌ Endpoint metadata only (no real ngtcp2 connection) node_saasm_extra.zig:6002 QuicEndpointHandle; 5940 quicNgTcp2Available is only dynLib detection
DTLS❌ Facade only (the plugin itself states handshake:false; record-layer encryption not modeled) node_saasm_extra.zig dtls_status_json self-disclosure
TLS server❌ Not implementedhttp_server has no TLS; node has no tls_server ABI

The same document's “one-sentence answer” summarizes: the truly usable end-to-end layers are TCP/UDP, HTTP/1+HTTPS, WebSocket, the H2 h2c client, the TLS client, and DNS; the layers whose real protocol machines are not connected are HTTP/3, QUIC, DTLS, the TLS server, the complete H2 server, and one-step H2-over-TLS.

NoteThe protocol matrix takes a joint four-plugin view: the TCP/UDP primitives come from sci's net.sa, and HTTP/1.x and WebSocket come from the http-client / http-server implementations compiled into libnode.so. Part of the node page's “network capability” is therefore essentially a restatement of the capabilities of http-client — HTTP Client and http-server — Embedded HTTP Server.

6. Installation and Verification

Development-time installation follows this chapter's uniform flow (executed in this plugin's directory; dependencies are installed together per sap.json):

# 在 D:/projects/sla/sa_plugin_node 内执行
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa plugin install --dev .
sa plugin list          # 确认 node 已安装
sa skills --json        # 确认 node.os / node.process / node.crypto /
                        # node.net / node.dns / node.http 六段已加载

The "Verification Commands" section of API_COVERAGE.md gives three official verification commands (verbatim):

zig build
zig build test
comm -23 <(rg '^@extern ' node.sai node_extra.sai | sed -E 's/.*@extern ([A-Za-z0-9_]+).*/\1/' | sort -u) \
         <(nm -D --defined-only zig-out/lib/libnode.so | awk '{print $3}' | sort -u)

The third is a contract audit: it lists “declared but not exported by the shared library” symbols; the ideal output is empty. In addition, the 188 .sa files under tests/ all carry an @test "…" annotation and @import "../node.sal", and can be run with the sa test workflow; progress.md also calls this "the native sa test workflow".

7. End-to-End Examples (Excerpted from Real Tests in the Repository)

The three excerpts below are all executable fragments from original repository files, with their sources marked in comments.

Example 1 — the os top-level facade four-piece set (D:/projects/sla/sa_plugin_node/tests/node_test_os_top.sa). It shows the status/exports/config/feature-support JSON snapshot usage that every module has, and the panic(103) convention on failure:

// SA tests for Node os top level facade helpers
@import "../node.sal"

@test "node.os top level facade helpers"():
L_ENTRY:
    status_ptr = add 0, 0
    status_len = add 0, 0
    s1 = add 0, 0
    EXPAND NODE_OS_STATUS_JSON status_ptr, status_len, s1
    ok1 = eq s1, 0
    br ok1 -> L_EXPORTS, L_ERR_STATUS
L_EXPORTS:
    !ok1
    exports_ptr = add 0, 0
    exports_len = add 0, 0
    s2 = add 0, 0
    EXPAND NODE_OS_TOP_EXPORTS_JSON exports_ptr, exports_len, s2
    ok2 = eq s2, 0
    br ok2 -> L_CONFIG, L_ERR_EXPORTS
// ……随后同样展开 NODE_OS_TOP_CONFIG_JSON、NODE_OS_TOP_FEATURE_SUPPORT_JSON，
//   最后对四个返回缓冲逐一 call @sa_node_plugin_free_buffer(ptr, len) 并 !掉中间值
L_ERR_STATUS:
    !ok1
    panic(103)

Example 2 — TCP listening and closing (tests/node_test_net_rw.sa, reproduced in full). Note the named-output style of the macros: srv is a handle output parameter, and s1/s2 are status output parameters:

// SA tests for Node net: listen, accept, connect, read, write
@import "../node.sal"
@const S_HOST = utf8:"127.0.0.1"
@const S_MSG = utf8:"hi"

@test "node.net listen and end"():
L_ENTRY:
    srv = add 0, 0
    s1 = add 0, 0
    s2 = add 0, 0
    EXPAND NODE_NET_LISTEN S_HOST, 9, 18769, srv, s1
    EXPAND NODE_NET_END srv, s2
    !s2
    !s1
    !srv
    return

Example 3 — real loopback UDP send/receive and buffer release (tests/node_test_dgram_recv.sa, excerpted; the ellipsis marks a second send/receive and release sequence for an empty-data datagram):

// SA tests for Node dgram: recv
@import "../node.sal"
@const S_HOST = utf8:"127.0.0.1"
@const S_MSG = utf8:"test"

@test "node.dgram recv"():
L_ENTRY:
    sock = add 0, 0
    EXPAND NODE_DGRAM_CREATE sock
    s1 = add 0, 0
    EXPAND NODE_DGRAM_BIND s1, sock, S_HOST, 9, 18771
    s2 = add 0, 0
    EXPAND NODE_DGRAM_SEND s2, sock, S_MSG, 4, S_HOST, 9, 18771
    op = add 0, 0        // payload 指针
    ol = add 0, 0        // payload 长度
    hp = add 0, 0        // 对端主机指针
    hl = add 0, 0
    port = add 0, 0
    s3 = add 0, 0
    EXPAND NODE_DGRAM_RECV s3, op, ol, hp, hl, port, sock, 1024
    // ……空数据报文 send/recv 分支略
    free_payload = call @sa_node_plugin_free_buffer(op, ol)
    free_host = call @sa_node_plugin_free_buffer(hp, hl)
    !free_payload
    !free_host
    // ……其余中间值 !略
    return

For path-style fs operation examples, see tests/node_test_fs_extra4.sa (NODE_FS_UNLINK / NODE_FS_RENAME / NODE_FS_RM, using fixed paths such as /tmp/sa_node_fs3.txt, which fall exactly inside the permission allowlist).

8. Explicit List of Unimplemented / Out-of-Scope Items

Completely excluded ("Explicitly Excluded" in API_COVERAGE.md, key points verbatim in substance): vm, v8, module loader execution, live inspector protocol/CDP sessions, debugger, and Node-internal bootstrap/realm behavior — because they require a JavaScript runtime or V8 semantics. repl keeps only the prompt/history/dot-command session subset and does no JavaScript evaluation.

Remaining Strict Node Gaps (same document, key points restated):

  • The full runtime semantics of HTTP/2 session/server/TLS ALPN/stream/push, QUIC/HTTP3 handshakes and session streams, the TLS socket/server object model, and DTLS handshakes and record-layer encryption all require mature native protocol library integration.
  • c-ares-level behavior (search domains/rotation/cancellation), real Promise object identity, and complete DNS error-code semantics are missing.
  • events/streams/timers/readline/worker_threads/ cluster/domain/test need a shared event loop + native callback dispatch model to reach strict Node behavior; strict timer ref/unref, AbortSignal cancellation, TTY raw behavior, and WHATWG stream locking/backpressure/pipe/tee/async iteration are all incomplete.
  • The WASI runtime (instantiation/start/initialize, the uvwasi syscall bridge, sandbox preopen enforcement), VFS asynchronous watch/event-emitter APIs, libffi variadic arguments and callbacks, SQLite session filtering/conflict callbacks, and Web Crypto RSA/ECDSA/ECDH/KDF/wrapKey/JWK all still need first-class ABI surfaces.
  • Node-compatible error classes/error codes and option validation are not yet complete across modules.

Structural limitations (from the permission ledger): even when a symbol exists, file access beyond $PROJECT/**//tmp/**, network connections to addresses other than port 18395, and child processes other than echo will be rejected by the host. The exec allowlist for child_process contains only echo, which means that module currently counts only as a placeholder implementation.

WarningThe "43/43 = 100%" self-rating in progress.md is in the facade dimension (the facades and metadata are written), not in the “the user's Node code runs through” dimension: the evaluation document “Four-Plugin Evaluation” (2026-06-15) explicitly notes the lack of a differential smoke test against real end-to-end Node scripts, and recommends treating node/deno as at least experimental in positioning. Before choosing it, please first self-test with the install commands on the Plugin Reference Overview page, then verify symbol landing with the contract audit command in Section 6.

path.join/resolveVariadic packing into a 16-byte {ptr,len} array ("argv", i.e. the plugin's SaSlice)
crypto.randomBytes/randomUUID, process.cwdsize/zero-argument + out-param
createHash/createHmac + update/digestHandle tracking (Map/Set precedent): update is folded via concat, digest uses the one-shot crypto_hash/hmac (hex native)
querystring.* / url.parse/format/resolveSingle/double slice; parse/format cross the boundary as JSON text
util.stripVTControlCharactersPure string→string (format/inspect/isDeepStrictEqual pieces missing, loudly rejected)
console.error/time/timeEnd/clearlog does not touch sa_std; the rest go through the plugin (a missing timer panics)
Buffer.byteLength/concatu64 output slot / static packing of literal elements (a dynamic array cannot hold slices, loudly rejected)
Deno.hostname/osRelease/readTextFile/writeTextFileSame shape (deno.sai; the harness-free list takes the sai as authoritative)
Deno.env.get/set/deleteTwo-level namespace routing; missing (status 1) maps to null (subset-consistent), any other non-zero value panics
6 asynchronous timers such as setTimeoutNo event loop, loudly rejected (a user's same-named definition takes precedence)

Discipline: anything outside the subset is loudly rejected (the base64 encoding in the timers-because-async and createHash chains, reuse after digest, etc.); Date goes through sa_std/time.sai (see the time: Clocks, Time, and Sleep page), not through this plugin. An import { a as b } alias is resolved via the remote name, and export default {..} / export default ns namespace objects reach definitions member by member (see satsgo todo/03_npm.md, measured on planck: 56 files linked in program caliber).
